question: Under rule 020101, appointments to public offices in the Federal Civil Service are made on the authority of which body?
options: The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
The Secretary to the Government of the Federation
explanation: Rule 020101: appointments are made on the authority of the Federal Civil Service Commission, by letter or by formal agreement.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020101

question: Under rule 020102(i), the Federal Civil Service Commission makes appointments to posts graded:
explanation: The Commission appoints to GL.12-17, as the need arises, into available vacancies after advertisement.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020102(i)

question: The annual competitive Civil Service Entry Examination under rule 020102(iv) is for posts graded:
explanation: The entry examination covers GL.07-10, for new entrants and serving officers wishing to transfer from other scheduled services.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020102(iv)

question: Under rule 020103, appointment of junior staff on GL.06 and below is handled by:
options: The Federal Civil Service Commission directly
The Office of the Head of the Civil Service of the Federation alone
The Junior Staff Committee of each Ministry/Extra-Ministerial Office, subject to the Permanent Secretary's approval
explanation: Each Ministry/Extra-Ministerial Office appoints junior staff through its Junior Staff Committee, with a representative of the Commission and the Head of Service present, subject to approval of the Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020103(a)

question: Under rule 020105, how long must an officer appointed or promoted have spent on the grade, with good performance, before enjoying the increment?
explanation: The incremental date is 1 January of every year, provided the officer has spent at least six months on the grade with good performance.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020105

question: Rule 020107 provides that the employment of unpaid staff is:
options: Permitted for a maximum of six months
explanation: Rule 020107: the employment of unpaid staff is prohibited.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020107

question: Under rule 020108(ii), alteration of the date of birth recorded on appointment is regarded as:
options: A permissible correction within the probationary period
explanation: The date of birth recorded on appointment shall not be changed throughout the officer's career; contravention is serious misconduct.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020108(ii)

question: Under rule 020205, an applicant for appointment into the Federal Public Service must be:
options: Not less than 16 and not more than 45 years of age
Not less than 21 and not more than 55 years of age
Not less than 18 and not more than 50 years of age
Not less than 18 and not more than 60 years of age
explanation: Rule 020205(a) sets the age band at 18 to 50 years.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020205(a)

question: Under rule 020206, which candidate may not be appointed without the Federal Civil Service Commission's prior specific approval?
options: One who holds a Higher National Diploma
One previously employed in government service and dismissed from it
One whose testimonial is from his last school
explanation: Prior approval is required if the candidate has been convicted of a criminal offence, or was previously dismissed or called upon to resign or retire from government service, irrespective of any delegation.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020206

question: Under rule 020211, contravention of the prohibition on membership of a secret society is regarded as:
options: Serious misconduct which may attract dismissal
Ordinary misconduct attracting a query only
A matter for the Code of Conduct Bureau only
explanation: Rule 020210 bars membership; rule 020211 treats contravention as serious misconduct that may include dismissal.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020210-020211

question: Under rule 020301, officers on probation are required to serve for:
explanation: Probation is two years before confirmation.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020301

question: Under rule 020301, the two-year probation may be reduced, by deducting previous satisfactory public service in posts of cognate status, to not less than:
explanation: The reduction is allowed down to a floor of six months.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020301

question: Under rule 020301, probation shall not exceed two years unless an extension is approved by:
options: The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
The Permanent Secretary of the Ministry
explanation: Any extension beyond two years needs the Commission's approval and may carry the incremental penalty in rule 040206.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020301

question: Under rule 020203(a), the normal period of service as a trainee or pupil is:
explanation: A trainee/pupil serves a normal two years in the post, which may be reduced in special circumstances.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020203(a)

question: Under rule 020401, a contract appointment is best described as:
options: A pensionable appointment for a specified period
An appointment of trainees for two years
A temporary appointment for a specific period that does not provide for payment of a pension
explanation: A contract appointment is a temporary, non-pensionable appointment for a specific period, recorded in a formal agreement.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020401

question: Under rule 020405, an officer on contract who desires re-engagement must inform government in writing not less than how long before his leave is due?
explanation: The notice is through the Permanent Secretary/Head of Extra-Ministerial Office, not less than four months before leave is due.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020405

question: Under rule 020411, retired officers may only be re-engaged into career posts on grade levels:
options: At the same level on which they retired
One level above that on which they retired
Any level approved by the Permanent Secretary
Immediately below that on which they retired
explanation: Re-engagement is restricted to the grade level immediately below the retirement level.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020411

question: Under rule 020501(b), secondment means:
options: The permanent release of an officer from one scheduled service to another
The posting of an officer outside his professional cadre
The temporary release of an officer to the service of another Government, approved body or recognised international organisation for a specified period
The grant of study leave to a confirmed officer
explanation: Secondment is a temporary release; transfer (rule 020501(a)) is the permanent release from one scheduled service to another.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020501

question: Under rule 020502(iv), the total period of secondment at an officer's own request must not exceed:
explanation: Secondment is two years in the first instance, with extensions approved by the committees and the Commission, and the total must not exceed four years.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020502(iv)

question: Under rule 020503(a), for a transfer from one senior post to another, an officer must first have served a minimum of how long in his original department?
explanation: Senior-post transfers need the Commission's prior approval and at least six months' service in the original department.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020503(a)

question: Under rule 020601, who approves a formal acting appointment, which is then gazetted?
options: The Head of the Civil Service of the Federation
The Permanent Secretary of the Ministry
The Secretary to the Government of the Federation
explanation: The Commission approves acting appointments, by notice in the gazette, for duty posts of status not lower than Senior Clerical Officer.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020601

question: Under rule 020604, an approved acting appointment shall not be back-dated to a period in excess of how long before the Commission received the recommendation?
explanation: Recommendations go on General Form 66, and back-dating is capped at six months from receipt.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020604

question: Under rule 020603, acting appointments are not intended as a means of:
options: Ensuring a duty post stays filled
Testing the suitability of officers for promotion
explanation: Acting appointments are not a form of trial promotion; they fill posts that are temporarily vacant and their duration should be limited.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020603

question: Under rule 020701(b), the minimum years an officer must spend in a post before being eligible for promotion on GL.06 and below, GL.07-14, and GL.15-17 are respectively:
explanation: The minimum is 2 years on GL.06 and below, 3 years on GL.07-14, and 4 years on GL.15-17.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020701(b)

question: Under rule 020701(d), promotion of officers on GL.15 - 17 is made by:
options: The Permanent Secretary of the officer's Ministry
The Federal Civil Service Commission, on recommendation routed through the Head of the Civil Service
explanation: GL.06 and below is by the Ministry; GL.07-14 is by the Ministry or relevant pool subject to confirmation by the Commission; GL.15-17 is by the Commission.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020701(d)

question: Under rule 020704, the effective date of all promotions is:
options: The date the promotion letter is signed
1 January of the year for which the promotion exercise was conducted, or as determined by the Commission
1 July of the year of the exercise
The date the officer passes the interview
explanation: Rule 020704 fixes 1 January of the exercise year unless the Commission determines otherwise.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020704

question: Under rule 020706, officers on approved leave of absence, secondment or special assignment:
options: Shall not be granted notional promotion and sit promotion examinations at designated centres nearest to them
Are automatically promoted on notional basis when peers are promoted
Are promoted by the Head of the Civil Service on return
explanation: Notional promotions are not granted; such officers sit promotion interviews/examinations at designated centres.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020706

question: Under rule 020707, an officer who has passed the compulsory examination for confirmation is eligible for promotion:
options: Only after completing the probationary period
Even though he has not completed the probationary period
Only after three years in service
Only with the Head of the Civil Service's special approval
explanation: Rule 020707 makes the officer eligible notwithstanding that probation under rule 020301 is incomplete.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020707

question: Under rule 020801, if an officer on probation is found not qualified for efficient service (and the cause is not misconduct), his appointment may be terminated by:
explanation: Provided termination is not due to misconduct, it is effected by a month's notice, with leave arranged within the notice period where applicable.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020801

question: Under rule 060203, an officer who fails the confirmation examination on three consecutive attempts is:
options: Required to resign or withdraw from the service
Placed on a further two-year probation
explanation: Three consecutive failures require the officer to resign or withdraw; the Permanent Secretary ensures compliance.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 060203

question: Under rule 060204, an officer who fails to take the confirmation examination after how long from first appointment is required to resign?
explanation: Failure to take the confirmation examination after 3 years of first appointment requires resignation from the service. (Rule 060206 separately requires GL.06 and below to take it within two years.)
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 060204; 060206

question: Under rule 020810(i), the compulsory retirement age for all grades is:
options: 60 years or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever is earlier
65 years or 40 years of service, whichever is earlier
60 years or 35 years of service, whichever is later
55 years or 30 years of service, whichever is earlier
explanation: Compulsory retirement is at 60 years of age or 35 years of pensionable service, whichever comes first.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020810(i)

question: Under rule 020810(iii), judicial officers and academic staff of universities retire at, respectively:
explanation: The 60/35 rule is without prejudice to prevailing requirements for judicial officers (70) and university academic staff (65).
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020810(iii)

question: Under rule 020810(iv) of the copy read, a Director shall compulsorily retire upon serving how many years on the post?
explanation: A Director retires after eight years on the post; a Permanent Secretary holds office for four years, renewable once for four more. Press reports place this rule at 021210 in PSR 2021 [secondary source: Leadership].
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 020810(iv); [secondary source: Leadership, Rule 021210 report]

question: Under rule 030103, the power of dismissal delegated to Permanent Secretaries and Heads of Extra-Ministerial Offices covers officers on:
explanation: Full disciplinary powers are delegated for GL.13 and below, except dismissal, which is delegated only for GL.06 and below.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030103

question: Under rule 030203, before proceedings for removal for general inefficiency may begin, the officer must have been warned in writing on how many occasions?
explanation: Rule 030203 requires three written warnings.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030203

question: Under rule 040205, an increment may be deferred for a period of:
options: Not less than three months nor more than six months
Not less than one month nor more than three months
Not less than six months nor more than twelve months
Not less than two months nor more than four months
explanation: A deferred increment not granted by six months from the original due date must be withheld.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 040205

question: Under rule 040204, which is the more serious penalty?
explanation: Rule 040204 states that to withhold an increment is more serious than to defer it.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 040204

question: Under rule 030208, in all cases of termination for inefficiency, the period of notice shall be:
options: One calendar month unless another period is appropriate to the officer's terms
explanation: Notice is one calendar month; if the officer leaves immediately, emolument equivalent to the notice period is paid.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030208

question: Which of the following is listed as misconduct (rather than serious misconduct) in rule 030301?
explanation: Habitual lateness is misconduct under 030301(c). Falsification, bribery and advance fee fraud are serious misconduct under 030402.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030301; 030402

question: Which of the following is listed as serious misconduct in rule 030402?
explanation: Falsification of records is serious misconduct; the others are listed as misconduct in rule 030301.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030402; 030301

question: Under rule 030404, an interdicted officer is paid:
options: Not more than half pay (50% of emoluments)
explanation: Interdiction is on not more than half pay pending determination of the case; if cleared, the officer is reinstated with full emoluments denied.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030404

question: Under rule 030406, an officer who is suspended pending investigation of serious misconduct receives:
options: No emolument for the period of suspension
explanation: Suspension is from the exercise of the powers and functions of office and from the enjoyment of emolument; it must not be used as a synonym for interdiction.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030406

question: Under rule 030307(xiii), disciplinary procedures must commence and be completed within:
options: 60 days, except where they involve criminal cases
explanation: Rule 030307(xiii) sets the 60-day limit, excluding criminal cases.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030307(xiii)

question: Which statement about a board of inquiry set up by the Commission under rule 030307 is correct?
options: It consists of not less than three persons, and the head of the officer's department shall not be a member
It consists of five persons including the head of the officer's department
The Commission itself hears the witnesses
The officer may not call witnesses
explanation: The Commission does not hear witnesses itself; the officer may call witnesses and put questions to those the board calls.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030307(v)-(ix)

question: Rule 030309 prohibits which of the following as punishment for an offence committed in the course of an officer's duties?
options: A surcharge for loss caused by neglect
explanation: No fine shall be imposed for an offence committed in the course of duties; surcharge is separately permitted under rule 030310.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030309; 030310

question: Under rule 030414(1)(a), an officer is deemed to be in serious financial embarrassment if his unsecured debts and liabilities at any time exceed:
explanation: Debts exceeding three times monthly emoluments, or being a judgement debtor or undischarged bankrupt, count as serious financial embarrassment.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030414(1)

question: Under rule 030423, an officer wishing to engage in partisan political activities or seek elective public office shall:
options: Be seconded to the political party
explanation: Resignation is necessary before seeking elective public office or engaging in partisan politics.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030423

question: Under rule 030424, a public officer may hold shares in companies but may not be:
options: A Director in a private company
A shareholder in a public company
A shareholder in a company operating abroad
A member of a cooperative society
explanation: Officers must not be directors in private companies and may be directors in public companies only if nominated by Government.
source: Public Service Rules (gazetted edition read), rule 030424(a)

question: Under the Federal Government circular of November 2022 on paternity leave in the Public Service Rules 2021 edition, paternity leave for serving male officers is:
explanation: The circular approved fourteen working days, also for an officer whose family adopts a child under four months old.
source: Circular 'Computation of Leave Based on Working Days and Approval of Paternity Leave in the Public Service', 25 Nov 2022, as reported by ThisDay/Radio Nigeria [secondary source]
